title: Euler-Twisted Hall Products, Green Coproducts, and Quantum Groups

items.title: The Hall-normalized extended positive Borel of a loopless quiver

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite loopless quiver over $\mathbb F_q$. Write $c_{ij}$ for
the number of arrows $i\to j$, set $\nu=\sqrt q>1$, and define the symmetric
Cartan matrix
$$ a_{ij}=2\delta_{ij}-c_{ij}-c_{ji}. $$
Let $\mathbb Q(\nu)$ be the coefficient field. Define the **extended
positive Borel algebra** $B_Q^+$ to be the $\mathbb Q(\nu)$-algebra generated
by $E_i$ and invertible commuting $K_i^{\pm1}$, with
$$ K_iK_i^{-1}=1, \qquad K_i E_jK_i^{-1}=\nu^{a_{ij}}E_j, $$
and, for $i\ne j$ and $m=1-a_{ij}$,
$$ \sum_{r=0}^{m}(-1)^r\binom{m}{r}_{\nu} E_i^{m-r}E_jE_i^r=0. $$
The Gaussian coefficients use the symmetric convention of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The formulas
$$ \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i, \qquad \Delta(K_i)=K_i\otimes K_i, $$
are the coproduct convention intended for this presentation; their
well-definedness on the defining relations is checked using
[[lem-coproduct-preserves-the-positive-and-negative-quantum-serre-ideals]].
The positive half is
the subalgebra generated by the $E_i$ alone; adjoining the $K_i^{\pm1}$ gives
the extended positive Borel.

items.title: A symmetric Gaussian alternating sum vanishes in the Serre range

references.title: Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, and let $d\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy
$1-m\le d\le m-1$ and $d\equiv m-1\pmod2$. With the symmetric Gaussian
binomial $C_{m,n}=\binom{m}{n}_{\nu}$ from
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]],
$$ \sum_{n=0}^{m}(-1)^n\nu^{-dn}C_{m, n}=0 $$
for every real $\nu>1$.
items.strategy: Rewrite the symmetric Gaussian coefficients by the ordinary q-binomial theorem; the stated parity and bounds force a factor 1−1.

items.title: A zero Yoneda splice factors through the middle object

references.title: Barry Mitchell, Theory of Categories, Chapter VII, §§4–5
Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §3.4, Yoneda Ext

items.statement:
Let $E$ be $0\to A\to B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ and let $F$ be
$0\to C\to D\to X\to0$ in an abelian category. If their splice is zero in
$\operatorname{YExt}^2(X,A)$, then there is an extension $G$ of $X$ by $B$
whose pushout along $p:B\to C$ is equivalent to $F$. Conversely every such
pushout has zero splice with $E$.

items.title: Low-degree exact sequences for Yoneda Ext in both variables

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §3.4, Yoneda Ext
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For a short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$
and an object $X$ in an abelian category, the sequence
$$ 0\to\operatorname{Hom}(X, A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X, B)\to \operatorname{Hom}(X, C)\xrightarrow{\delta} \operatorname{YExt}^1(X, A)\to\operatorname{YExt}^1(X, B)\to \operatorname{YExt}^1(X, C)\xrightarrow{\partial} \operatorname{YExt}^2(X, A) $$
is exact at every term before the final $\operatorname{YExt}^2$ term. The
boundary $\delta$ pulls back the given extension along a map $X\to C$;
$\partial$ splices it with a short extension of $X$ by $C$. The dual sequence
in the first Ext variable is exact at the corresponding terms:
$$ 0\to\operatorname{Hom}(C, X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B, X)\to \operatorname{Hom}(A, X)\to\operatorname{YExt}^1(C, X)\to \operatorname{YExt}^1(B, X)\to\operatorname{YExt}^1(A, X)\to \operatorname{YExt}^2(C, X). $$

items.title: Finite-field hereditary Hall categories

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement:
A **finite-field hereditary Hall category** is a supplied small
$\mathbb F_q$-linear abelian category $\mathcal A$ with the following
properties:

1. For every pair $M,N$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,N)$ is a
   finite-dimensional $\mathbb F_q$-vector space and the Yoneda extension
   group $\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)$ is finite-dimensional over
   $\mathbb F_q$. Its addition is Baer sum; scalar multiplication by
   $\lambda\in\mathbb F_q$ is pushout along $\lambda\operatorname{id}_N$.
2. For every $M,N$, $\operatorname{YExt}^2(M,N)=0$, where a two-fold
   extension is an exact sequence $0\to N\to E_1\to E_0\to M\to0$
   modulo endpoint-fixed chain-map equivalence
   ([[def-n-fold-yoneda-extension]],
   [[def-equivalence-of-n-fold-extensions]]).
3. Smallness and the finiteness conditions of the Hall definition hold
   ([[def-hall-finitary-abelian-category]]).

Here $\mathbb F_q$-linear means that every Hom set is a vector space and
composition is bilinear. “Hereditary” in this page means exactly the stated
vanishing of Yoneda $\operatorname{Ext}^2$; no projective or injective
resolutions, derived-Ext identification, or choice principle is built into
the definition. Under these conditions the Euler form used below is
$$ \langle[M],[N]\rangle=\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N) -\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N). $$

items.title: Finite-dimensional representations of an acyclic quiver form a hereditary finitary Hall category

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite acyclic quiver and $k=\mathbb F_q$. A representation is
finite-dimensional at every vertex, with one linear map for each arrow. The
category $\operatorname{Rep}_k(Q)$ is a small hereditary finitary abelian
category in the sense of
[[def-finite-field-hereditary-hall-category]]. Its simple objects are the
vertex representations $S_i$, its Grothendieck group is freely generated by
$[S_i]$ and is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$, and
$$ \dim_k\operatorname{YExt}^1(S_i, S_j)=c_{ij}, $$
where $c_{ij}$ is the number of arrows $i\to j$.
For any two representations $V,W$, its Euler form is explicitly
$$ \langle[V],[W]\rangle =\sum_{i\in Q_0}\dim V_i\dim W_i -\sum_{a:i\to j}\dim V_i\dim W_j. $$
items.strategy: Use the explicit length-one path resolution by finite-dimensional representable projectives, then count finite-dimensional representations and maps over the finite field.

items.title: Finite loopless quiver nilpotent representation categories are hereditary and finitary

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite loopless quiver over $\mathbb F_q$. If $Q$ has oriented
cycles, take the abelian category of finite-dimensional nilpotent
representations; if $Q$ is acyclic, take all finite-dimensional
representations. This category is a small finite-field hereditary Hall
category. Its simple objects are $S_i$, $K_0\cong\mathbb Z^{Q_0}$ by dimension
vector, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{YExt}^1(S_i,S_j)=c_{ij}$ for
arrows $i\to j$.

items.title: The hereditary Euler form is additive on the Grothendieck group

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §3.4, Yoneda Ext

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category. For objects
$M,N$, define
$$ \langle[M],[N]\rangle =\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N) -\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N). $$
This form is additive in short exact sequences in either variable, so it
descends to a well-defined bilinear form on $K_0(\mathcal A)$.
items.strategy: Apply the two low-degree Yoneda exact sequences and take alternating dimensions.

items.title: Exact-sequence counts equal endpoint automorphism counts times subobject counts

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a small finitary abelian category and let
$M,N,R\in\mathcal A$. Let $P^R_{M,N}$ be the number of endpoint-labelled
short exact sequences $0\to N\to R\to M\to0$, and let
$a_X=|\operatorname{Aut}(X)|$. Then
$$ P^R_{M, N}=a_Ma_Ng^R_{M, N}, $$
where $g^R_{M,N}$ counts subobjects $N\hookrightarrow R$ with quotient
isomorphic to $M$ as in [[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]].
items.strategy: Use the free endpoint-automorphism action on exact sequences; its orbits are exactly the counted subobject classes.

items.title: The Euler-twisted Hall algebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category over
$\mathbb F_q$, and choose the positive square root $\nu=\sqrt q$. For
objects $M,N$, put
$\chi_0(M,N)=\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)-
\dim_{\mathbb F_q}\operatorname{YExt}^1(M,N)$. This integer depends only on
the isomorphism classes of $M,N$. At this point $\chi_0$ is only an
object-level exponent; additivity on $K_0$ and the resulting bicharacter are
separate proof obligations. The coefficient field is $\mathbb Q(\nu)$. The
**Euler-twisted Hall algebra** is the graded
vector
space
$$ H_{\mathcal A,\nu}=\bigoplus_{[M]}\mathbb Q(\nu)[M],\qquad \deg[M]=[M]\in K_0(\mathcal A), $$
with bilinear operation
$$ [M]\star[N] =\nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}\sum_{[L]}g^L_{M,N}[L], $$
where [[def-untwisted-hall-algebra]] fixes
$0\to N\to L\to M\to0$. This operation is distinct from the untwisted
product: its field, Euler exponent and square-root parameter are additional
data. Finite support and associativity are verified in the following items.

items.title: The Euler-twisted Hall product is well-defined

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement:
For a finite-field hereditary Hall category, the basis formula in
[[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]] has finite support and defines a
$\mathbb Q(\nu)$-bilinear operation on the direct-sum Hall space.
items.strategy: Multiply each finite untwisted Hall coefficient and support by the fixed Euler scalar.

items.title: The Green Hall completion and coproduct

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category and use
$H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$ and the object-level integer $\chi_0(M,N)$ from
[[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]]. For a basis object $R$, let
$P^R_{M,N}$ count endpoint-labelled exact sequences
$0\to N\to R\to M\to0$, and put $a_R=|\operatorname{Aut}(R)|$. Define the
**coefficientwise completed tensor space**
$$ H_{\mathcal A,\nu}\widehat\otimes H_{\mathcal A,\nu} =\prod_{([M],[N])}\mathbb Q(\nu)\,([M]\otimes[N]), $$
the space of all coefficient functions on ordered pairs of isomorphism
classes. Define the Green coproduct and counit by
$$ \Delta'([R])=\sum_{[M],[N]} \nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}\frac{P^R_{M,N}}{a_R}[M]\otimes[N], \qquad \epsilon([R])=\begin{cases}1,&R\cong0,\\0,&R\not\cong0.\end{cases} $$
Each coefficient is finite; the sum need not have finite support. On finite
pure tensors define the **Euler-twisted tensor multiplication** by
$$ ([X]\otimes[Y])\cdot([Z]\otimes[W]) =\nu^{\chi_0(Y,Z)+\chi_0(Z,Y)}([X]\star[Z])\otimes([Y]\star[W]). $$
It is extended to completed tensors only when every output coefficient is a
finite sum. No algebra structure on the whole completion is asserted; this
finite-convergence condition is proved for products of Green images below.

items.title: The Euler-twisted Hall product is associative and unital

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
The operation of [[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]] is a well-defined
associative $\mathbb Q(\nu)$-bilinear product with unit $[0]$.
items.strategy: Use additivity of the Euler form to check the twist cocycle and then the untwisted Hall associativity.

items.title: Green coproduct coefficients are finite

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For fixed objects $R,M,N$ in a finite-field hereditary Hall category, the
endpoint-labelled count $P^R_{M,N}$ and hence the coefficient of
$[M]\otimes[N]$ in [[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]] are finite.
This assertion does not claim finite support in $[M],[N]$ for a fixed $R$.
items.strategy: Bound endpoint-labelled sequences by the finite product Hom(N,R)×Hom(R,M).

items.title: The Green cross–square counting identity

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category. Write
$a_X=|\operatorname{Aut}(X)|$, and let $P^R_{M,N}$ count exact sequences
$0\to N\to R\to M\to0$. For fixed objects $M,N,K,L$, the following
cross–square identity holds:
$$ \sum_{[J]}\frac{P^J_{M,N}P^J_{K,L}}{a_J} =\sum_{[K_1],[K_2],[L_1],[L_2]} \frac{|\operatorname{YExt}^1(K_2,L_1)|} {|\operatorname{Hom}(K_2,L_1)|} \frac{P^K_{K_2,K_1}P^L_{L_2,L_1}P^M_{K_2,L_2}P^N_{K_1,L_1}} {a_{K_1}a_{K_2}a_{L_1}a_{L_2}}. $$
Both sums are finite. The left side counts pairs of exact sequences with a
common middle object $J$; the right side counts the compatible four-edge
square data, weighted by the displayed Yoneda Ext/Hom ratio.

The diagrams below display the data being counted. A **cross** is a pair of
short exact sequences with the same middle object; it is not an assertion of
vertical maps between the endpoint objects.

```tikzcd
0 \arrow[r] & N \arrow[r, tail, "n"] & J \arrow[r, two heads, "b"] & M \arrow[r] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & L \arrow[r, tail, "\ell"] & J \arrow[r, two heads, "b'"] & K \arrow[r] & 0
```

A **square datum** is the isomorphism class of these four exact edges:
$$ 0\to L_1\to N\to K_1\to0, \quad 0\to L_1\to L\to L_2\to0, \quad 0\to K_1\to K\to K_2\to0, \quad 0\to L_2\to M\to K_2\to0. $$

```tikzcd
0 \arrow[r] & L_1 \arrow[r, tail] \arrow[d, equal] & N \arrow[r, two heads] & K_1 \arrow[r] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & L_1 \arrow[r, tail] & L \arrow[r, two heads] & L_2 \arrow[r] & 0
\\[1.2em]
0 \arrow[r] & K_1 \arrow[r, tail] & K \arrow[r, two heads] \arrow[d, equal] & K_2 \arrow[r] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & L_2 \arrow[r, tail] & M \arrow[r, two heads] & K_2 \arrow[r] & 0
```

The equal labels indicate shared endpoint isomorphism classes only; no
additional morphisms between the two rows are part of the square datum.
items.strategy: Take kernels, images, and cokernels in each cross, then count completions by the Yoneda exact sequence and explicit automorphism stabilizers.

items.title: The extended Hall algebra and composition subalgebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category and let
$K_0=K_0(\mathcal A)$. Put
$([\alpha],[\beta])=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle+
\langle\beta,\alpha\rangle$. The **extended Hall algebra** is the vector
space $\widetilde H=\mathbb Q(\nu)[K_0]\otimes H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$ with
basis $k_\alpha[M]$ and multiplication
$$ (k_\alpha[M])(k_\beta[N]) =\nu^{-(\beta,[M])}k_{\alpha+\beta}([M]\star[N]). $$
The notation is left-torus normal order: $k_\alpha[M]$ is the actual product of the torus and Hall elements. Thus moving $k_\beta$ past $[M]$ contributes $\nu^{-(\beta,[M])}$. Equivalently, $k_\alpha k_\beta=k_{\alpha+\beta}$ and
$k_\alpha[M]k_\alpha^{-1}=\nu^{(\alpha,[M])}[M]$. Associativity follows
from the bilinearity of the symmetric Euler form and the associative Hall
product; the toral action is checked in
[[lem-extended-hall-torus-action-is-well-defined]].

If $\mathcal A$ has a specified set of simple objects $\{S_i\}$, the
**composition subalgebra** is the subalgebra of $H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$
generated by $[S_i]$. Its extension by all $k_\alpha$ is the **extended
composition subalgebra**.

items.title: The extended Hall torus action is well-defined

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For each $\alpha\in K_0$, the map on homogeneous Hall elements
$x\mapsto\nu^{(\alpha,\deg x)}x$ is an algebra automorphism. Hence the
cross-relations in [[def-extended-hall-algebra-and-composition-subalgebra]]
define an associative crossed-product algebra.
items.strategy: Use K_0 grading of Hall products and biadditivity of the symmetric Euler form.

items.title: The Green Hall coproduct is coassociative

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
The Green coproduct $\Delta'$ of
[[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]] is coassociative in the
coefficientwise completion, with counit $\epsilon$ as defined there.
items.strategy: Identify both triple coefficients with the same two-step flags and compare the bilinear Euler weights.

items.title: Products of Green coproducts converge coefficientwise

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For any $M,N$, the product $\Delta'([M])\cdot\Delta'([N])$ in the twisted
tensor multiplication of [[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]] has a
finite coefficient sum at every fixed basis pair $[R]\otimes[S]$. Thus the
product is defined in the coefficientwise completion. The claim does not
extend to arbitrary pairs of completed tensors.
items.strategy: Use the finite Hom sets to determine the relevant image subobjects in any contributing diagram.

items.title: Green’s coproduct is an algebra map into the twisted tensor completion

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement:
For a finite-field hereditary Hall category, products of Green images converge
coefficientwise and
$$ \Delta'([M]\star[N])=\Delta'([M])\cdot\Delta'([N]) $$
in the completion of [[def-green-hall-completion-and-coproduct]], where the
target multiplication is the stated Euler-twisted tensor multiplication. The
coproduct is coassociative and counital by
[[lem-green-hall-coproduct-is-coassociative]]. It is not asserted that the
whole completion is an algebra.
items.strategy: Expand both sides on basis elements, reduce coefficients to the cross-square count, and verify coefficientwise convergence.

items.title: The Green Hall pairing is nondegenerate and adjoint to product and coproduct

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
On the direct-sum Hall space define
$$ ([M],[N])_G=\frac{\delta_{[M],[N]}}{a_M}. $$
This bilinear form is nondegenerate over $\mathbb Q(\nu)$ and satisfies
$$ ([M]\star[N],[R])_G =([M]\otimes[N],\Delta'([R]))_{G\otimes G}, $$
where the tensor pairing is the product of the two Green pairings.
items.strategy: Evaluate both pairings on basis elements and use the exact-sequence normalization.

items.title: The extended Green coproduct is an algebra map

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For the extended Hall algebra of
[[def-extended-hall-algebra-and-composition-subalgebra]], define
$\Delta_-(k_\alpha)=k_\alpha\otimes k_\alpha$ and, for homogeneous $[R]$,
$$ \Delta_-([R]) =\sum_{[M],[N]}\nu^{\langle M,N\rangle} \frac{P^R_{M,N}}{a_R}\,[M]\otimes k_{-[M]}[N]. $$
Then $\Delta_-$ is an algebra map into the coefficientwise completed tensor
space of the extended Hall algebra, with ordinary (untwisted) tensor
multiplication on the coproduct images, whose coefficient sums converge.
The counit is an algebra map to the coefficient field. If every basis
coproduct has finite support, these maps define an ordinary tensor-product
bialgebra; otherwise their target is the stated completion. This is the **DJ-compatible extended Green convention** used on this
page. The alternative formula
$\Delta_+([R])=\sum c^R_{M,N}[M]k_{[N]}\otimes[N]$ has
$\Delta_+([S_i])=[S_i]\otimes1+k_i\otimes[S_i]$ and is kept separate.
items.strategy: Check the group-like and Hall generators and use the torus action to convert the twisted tensor factor into the extended tensor product.

items.title: The extended Green and repository Drinfeld–Jimbo coproduct conventions agree on simple generators

references.title: Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For a vertex simple $S_i$, the DJ-compatible extended Green coproduct has
$$ \Delta_-([S_i])=[S_i]\otimes k_i^{-1}+1\otimes[S_i], $$
which is exactly the repository Drinfeld–Jimbo coproduct formula on $E_i$.
The alternative Hall convention
$\Delta_+([S_i])=[S_i]\otimes1+k_i\otimes[S_i]$ is distinct and is not
silently identified with $\Delta_-$. The positive Borel coproduct formulas
are well-defined at $\nu=\sqrt q>1$.
items.strategy: Evaluate the extended Green formula on a simple object and compare the two generator coproducts term by term.

items.title: The Ringel assignment is a bialgebra homomorphism onto the extended composition subalgebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement:
For a finite loopless quiver $Q$ over $\mathbb F_q$, using nilpotent
finite-dimensional representations when $Q$ has oriented cycles, the
assignment
$$ E_i\longmapsto[S_i],\qquad K_i^{\pm1}\longmapsto k_{\pm e_i} $$
defines a surjective bialgebra homomorphism from the extended positive Borel
of [[def-quiver-hall-positive-borel]] onto the extended composition
subalgebra of [[def-extended-hall-algebra-and-composition-subalgebra]]. The
claim does not include injectivity.
items.strategy: Check the symmetric Cartan action, count simple filtrations to verify every Serre coefficient, and compare the group-like coproduct formulas.

items.title: Prime-power specializations of the integral quantum half have a nondegenerate Green form
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice of the global-basis suppliers. Let $I$ be a finite symmetric Cartan datum with symmetrizers $d_i=1$; its generalized Cartan matrix need not be of finite type. Write $A=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, and let $U_A^-$ denote the divided-power integral half inside the generic quantum Serre algebra over $\mathbb Q(t)$. Let $Q=p^a>1$ be a prime power, let $\nu=\sqrt Q>1$, and set $K=\mathbb Q(\nu)$ and $H_\pm=K\otimes_{A,t\mapsto\nu^{\pm1}}U_A^-$.

The normalized Kashiwara form $B_t$ specializes to a nondegenerate symmetric form on every finite homogeneous component of both $H_+$ and $H_-$. Their component dimensions are the classical PBW ranks. On $H_-$ the primitive-generator coproduct has tensor multiplication
$$ (x\otimes y)(x'\otimes y')=\nu^{(\deg y,\deg x')}xx'\otimes yy'. $$
The rescaled homogeneous form $G(x,y)=(Q-1)^{-\operatorname{ht}\alpha}B_{\nu^{-1}}(x,y)$ for $x,y\in H_-[-\alpha]$, zero in different degrees, has $G(F_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(Q-1)$ and both braided Hopf adjunctions. Thus it has exactly the generator values and symmetric tensor twist of the Green pairing.

This statement concerns the specialization of the integral half. It does not identify that algebra with the algebra presented at the numerical parameter by the quantum Serre relations alone.

items.title: Green positivity specializes the integral half into the composition algebra
items.statement:
Let $Q=p^a>1$, $\nu=\sqrt Q$, and $K=\mathbb Q(\nu)\subset\mathbb R$. Let $\mathcal H$ be the real twisted Hall algebra of the finite-dimensional nilpotent representations of a finite loopless quiver over $\mathbb F_Q$; an acyclic quiver needs no nilpotence restriction. Write $u_i=[S_i]$ for its vertex simples and $C_K$ for the $K$-algebra they generate. Let $A=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]$, and let $U_A^-$ be the generic divided-power integral half for the symmetric matrix $a_{ij}=2\delta_{ij}-(\text{number of arrows joining }i,j)$.

There is a surjective graded algebra map
$$\Psi:K\otimes_{A,t\mapsto\nu^{-1}}U_A^-\longrightarrow C_K,\qquad F_i\longmapsto u_i.$$
It preserves the homogeneous form $(Q-1)^{-\operatorname{ht}\alpha}B_{\nu^{-1}}$. In particular $\dim_K C_K[\alpha]$ is at most the classical PBW rank. This conclusion requires only positive Green pairing and the generic word-form identity, and does not require specialized nondegeneracy or any numerical Serre-presentation comparison.

items.title: Reflection classifies finite-Dynkin quiver indecomposables over a finite field
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from finite-root suppliers. Let $Q$ be a finite acyclic quiver and $k=\mathbb F_q$. At a sink $i$
define the reflection functor on a representation $M$ by replacing $M_i$ with
$\ker(\bigoplus_{j\to i}M_j\to M_i)$ and reversing the incident arrows
using its kernel projections. At a source use the dual cokernel functor.
These are inverse exact equivalences between the full subcategories with no
$S_i$ direct summand. They commute with field extension.

If the underlying graph is a finite ADE forest, the dimension map gives a bijection from the indecomposable $kQ$-modules
to the positive roots of the componentwise finite root system. Every
indecomposable is absolutely indecomposable, has endomorphism ring $k$ and
self-$\operatorname{Ext}^1=0$. There is an ordering $M_1,\ldots,M_m$ of
these indecomposables with
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M_j,M_i)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(M_i,M_j)=0\qquad(i<j).$$
Here representations are finite-dimensional; there are no oriented cycles,
so path nilpotence is automatic.

items.title: Finite-Dynkin Hall algebras are generated by vertex simples
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be any orientation of a finite ADE forest over $k=\mathbb F_q$,
with $\nu=\sqrt q>1$ and coefficient field $\mathbb Q(\nu)$.
Its Euler-twisted Hall algebra is generated by the vertex-simple classes.
Consequently its composition algebra equals the full positive Hall algebra,
and adjoining the declared Cartan torus gives the full extended Hall algebra.
No fixed-parameter quantum-group injectivity theorem or Hall polynomial
existence theorem is a premise.

items.title: Finite-field descent and restriction of Schur quiver representations
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite quiver, $k=\mathbb F_q$, and $\overline k$ an algebraic
closure. A finite-dimensional representation $M$ over $\overline k$ is
called Schur here when $\operatorname{End}_{\overline k Q}M=\overline k$.
Let $\mathscr S$ be a Frobenius-stable set of Schur geometric isomorphism
classes of a fixed dimension vector $\delta$, consisting of representations
defined over some finite extensions. Every class fixed by the $m$th
Frobenius power has a model over $k_m=\mathbb F_{q^m}$, unique up to
$k_m$-isomorphism. If constants $c,C>0$ satisfy
$$c q^m\le|\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{Fr}^m;\mathscr S)|\le Cq^m$$
for all sufficiently large $m$, then for all sufficiently large $m$ there
are at least $c' q^m/m$ pairwise nonisomorphic indecomposable
$kQ$-representations of dimension $m\delta$, for a constant $c'>0$.
This conclusion also holds within the nilpotent representation category
when the classes in $\mathscr S$ are nilpotent.

items.title: Explicit affine D and E flag families give exponentially many indecomposables
items.statement:
Let $Q$ have underlying graph an affine tree of type
$\widetilde D_n$ ($n\ge4$), $\widetilde E_6$, $\widetilde E_7$ or
$\widetilde E_8$, with any orientation, over $k=\mathbb F_q$.
Let $\delta$ be its primitive positive null vector. There are constants
$c>0,m_0$ such that for every $m\ge m_0$ the category has at least
$cq^m/m$ pairwise nonisomorphic indecomposable representations of dimension
$m\delta$. All its representations are nilpotent, since the underlying
graph is a tree. The construction uses only partial flags, finite-field
descent and source/sink reflection, not a classification of arbitrary
quiver indecomposables.

For $\widetilde D$, $\delta$ has value $2$ along the central chain and
$1$ on its four outer leaves. For $\widetilde E$, use the star with arm
types $(p,q,r)=(3,3,3),(2,4,4),(2,3,6)$, respectively. The central value is
$N=3,4,6$, and the arm values, from the outside inward, are
$N/s,2N/s,\ldots,(s-1)N/s$ for an arm of type $s$.

items.title: The full Hall algebra is simple-generated exactly in componentwise finite Dynkin type
items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite loopless quiver over $k=\mathbb F_q$, using
finite-dimensional nilpotent representations when oriented cycles occur,
and use the Euler-twisted Hall algebra over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)$.
Its vertex-simple-generated composition subalgebra equals the full Hall
algebra if and only if every connected component of the underlying
multigraph is a finite ADE Dynkin diagram. Thus adjoining the declared
Cartan torus gives the full extended Hall algebra exactly under the same
componentwise finite-type condition. The empty quiver is included.

No injectivity theorem for the Ringel map is a premise. The only quantum
rank input is the independent surjection from the specialized divided-power
integral half onto the composition algebra, which supplies an upper bound
by classical PBW ranks.

items.title: Rank-one skew kernels in a numerical quantum Serre algebra
items.statement:
Let $I$ be finite, $A=(a_{jk})$ a symmetric generalized Cartan matrix, and $q>1$ a real number. Let $S$ be the complex associative algebra on generators $e_j$ for $j\in I$, with only the numerical quantum Serre relations
$$ \sum_{s=0}^{N+1}(-1)^s{N+1\brack s}_q e_j^{N+1-s}e_ke_j^s=0,\qquad j\ne k,\quad N=-a_{jk}. $$
Here $[r]_q=(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$, divided powers are $e_j^{(n)}=e_j^n/[n]_q!$, and $S$ is graded by $\deg e_j=\alpha_j$. Fix $i\in I$ and write $m(\beta)=\sum_j a_{ij}\beta_j$ for a root degree $\beta=\sum_j\beta_j\alpha_j$.

The operators on words specified by
$$ D(e_j)=D'(e_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad D(xy)=D(x)y+q^{m(\deg x)}xD(y),\quad D'(xy)=q^{m(\deg y)}D'(x)y+xD'(y) $$
descend to $S$, commute, and are locally nilpotent. Set $B_i=\ker D$. Then
$$ S=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}e_i^{(n)}B_i. $$
For homogeneous $b\in B_i$ put
$$ R(b)=e_i b-q^{-m(\deg b)}b e_i,\qquad F(b)=-\frac{D'(b)}{q-q^{-1}},\qquad K(b)=q^{m(\deg b)}b. $$
These define an integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action on $B_i$, with conventions $KRK^{-1}=q^2R$, $KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}F$, and $RF-FR=(K-K^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$. The algebra $B_i$ is generated by the finite root strings $R^r(e_j)$, $j\ne i$, $0\leq r\leq-a_{ij}$. In particular, if $0\ne z\in S_\beta$ satisfies $D(z)=D'(z)=0$, then $m(\beta)\leq0$.

items.title: The nondegenerate integral specialization has a quantum Casimir
items.statement:
Let $
u=\sqrt{p^a}>1$, $K=\mathbb Q(
u)$, and let $U$ be the actual specialization at $t=
u$ of the Lusztig integral form for a finite symmetric Cartan datum, extended to a regular realization. Use the source coproduct $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes F_i$. Its two halves are the actual integral specializations, without any numerical Serre-only presentation assertion. Write $Q= igoplus_i\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ and put $f(\lambda)=(\lambda,\lambda)+2\sum_i n_i$ for $\lambda=\sum_i n_i\alpha_i\in Q$.

On every $Q$-label-graded $U$-module whose weights lie in a finite union of translates of $-Q_+$, there is a natural operator $\mathcal C$, commuting with $U$, such that its action on a highest-weight vector of label $\lambda\in Q$ is $
u^{f(\lambda)}$. Consequently it acts by $1$ on each Verma module $M_U(-\alpha_i)$ and its subquotients. A nonzero highest-weight vector of label $- eta$ in a subquotient of $ igoplus_i M_U(-\alpha_i)$ must satisfy $( eta, eta)=2\operatorname{ht} eta$.

items.title: A minimal numerical Serre kernel obeys the quantum Casimir constraint
items.statement:
Use $U,K,
u,Q$ from [[lem-the-nondegenerate-integral-specialization-has-a-quantum-casimir]]. Let $T=K\langle F_i:i\in Iangle$ be the free negative tensor algebra, let $J=\ker(T	o U^-)$, and let $S\subseteq J$ be its two-sided numerical quantum Serre ideal. If $J/S
e0$ and $ eta\in Q_+$ has least height with $(J/S)[- eta]
e0$, then
$$ ( eta, eta)=2\operatorname{ht} eta>0. $$
The quantum Casimir is used only on the already established actual integral specialization, whose pairing is nondegenerate; it is not assumed to act on the numerical Serre-only algebra.

items.title: The prime-power numerical Serre half is the integral specialization
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Choice hypothesis of the integral/global-basis suppliers. Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a symmetric generalized Cartan matrix on a finite index set; finite, affine and indefinite type are all allowed. Let $
u=\sqrt{p^a}>1$, $K=\mathbb Q(
u)\subset\mathbb R$, and $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. The algebra over $K$ on generators $E_i$ with only the symmetric numerical quantum Serre relations at parameter $
u^\epsilon$ is canonically isomorphic, by $E_i\mapsto E_i$, to the actual Lusztig integral-half specialization $K\otimes_{\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}],t\mapsto
u^\epsilon}U_A^+$. Its finite homogeneous components have the classical PBW ranks and the nondegenerate specialized half form. For the primitive braided tensor twist $
u^{(\alpha, eta)}$, the form with $G(E_i,E_j)=\delta_{ij}/(p^a-1)$ is nondegenerate and satisfies both Hopf adjunctions.

items.title: The Ringel map embeds the extended positive Borel and is full Hall exactly in finite Dynkin type

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the quantum global-basis suppliers. Let $Q$ be a finite loopless quiver over $\mathbb F_q$, using finite-dimensional
nilpotent representations when $Q$ has oriented cycles. The assignment
$E_i\mapsto[S_i]$, $K_i\mapsto k_i$ embeds the extended positive Borel for
the symmetric Cartan matrix of the underlying graph into the extended Hall
algebra, with image the torus extension of the composition subalgebra. Its
positive half maps onto the full Hall algebra exactly when the underlying
graph is finite Dynkin, meaning that each connected component is a finite ADE Dynkin diagram (including the empty graph).

items.title: The Kronecker Hall algebra strictly contains its composition subalgebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement:
For the two-arrow Kronecker quiver, the degree $(1,1)$ Hall component has
$q+2$ basis classes, whereas its simple-generated composition subalgebra has
dimension at most two in that degree. Thus the full Hall algebra is strictly
larger than the composition subalgebra.

```tikzcd
1 \arrow[r, shift left=0.7ex, "a"]
  \arrow[r, shift right=0.7ex, swap, "b"] & 2
```

The diagram denotes two distinct parallel arrows from vertex $1$ to vertex
$2$. A representation assigns a scalar to each arrow when both vertex spaces
are one-dimensional.
items.strategy: Classify dimension-(1,1) representations by a pair of arrow scalars modulo endpoint rescaling and count the two simple-generator words.

items.title: A one-vertex Green coproduct and twisted Hall square

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement:
For the one-vertex zero-arrow quiver, with simple $S$ and
$R=S\oplus S$, compute
$$ [S]\star[S]=\nu(q+1)[R],\qquad \Delta'([S])=[S]\otimes[0]+[0]\otimes[S], $$
and
$$ \Delta'([R])=[R]\otimes[0]+[0]\otimes[R] +\nu^{-1}[S]\otimes[S]. $$

For this example, $\Delta'$ means the coefficient formula
$\Delta'([T])=\sum_{A,B}\nu^{\dim A\dim B}P^T_{A,B}a_T^{-1}[A]\otimes[B]$;
it is the one-vertex specialization of Green’s definition. The product is
$[A]\star[B]=\nu^{\dim A\dim B}[A]*[B]$.

```tikzpicture
\node[draw,circle] (v) {$1$};
```

This is the quiver with one vertex and no arrows.
items.strategy: Count the lines in F_q^2 and the endpoint-labelled exact sequences with middle F_q^2.

items.title: The A2 Hall products and their quantum Serre relation

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement:
For the one-arrow quiver $1\to2$, let $S_1,S_2$ be its simples and let $I$
be the nonzero-arrow representation of dimension $(1,1)$. Then
$$ [S_1]\star[S_2]=\nu^{-1}([S_1\oplus S_2]+[I]),\qquad [S_2]\star[S_1]=[S_1\oplus S_2], $$
and in degree $(2,1)$ the divided-power Serre relation is
$$ [S_1]^{(2)}\star[S_2]-[S_1]\star[S_2]\star[S_1] +[S_2]\star[S_1]^{(2)}=0. $$
Here $x^{(2)}=x^2/[2]_\nu!$ as in
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

```tikzcd
1 \arrow[r, "a"] & 2
```
